Sardius
SAR-dee-us
noun
Greek sardios (G4556), Hebrew odem (H124) — a deep blood-red precious stone, identified today as carnelian or red jasper; the sixth foundation of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:20). The stone is named after Sardis, the city in Asia Minor (one of the seven churches of Asia, Rev 3:1-6) where rich deposits of the stone were mined.

📖 Biblical Definition

Sardius is the sixth foundation stone of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:20), the first stone of the high priest's breastplate (Exod 28:17; 39:10), one of the precious stones covering the anointed cherub in Eden (Ezek 28:13), and — most weighty of all — the first half of the appearance of God Himself on the throne in John's vision: "He that sat was to look upon LIKE A JASPER AND A SARDINE STONE" (Rev 4:3). The deep blood-red of sardius pictures the wrath and judgment of God; sardius first, then jasper (clear glory) — but the order in Revelation 4:3 may be deliberate: God's throne appears red-and-clear together, judgment glowing through holiness. The OT breastplate carried sardius as the FIRST stone — the first tribe in the priestly order (Reuben in most reconstructions) — pictured by the stone that represents the cost of approach to God. The New Jerusalem's sixth foundation is the same stone: the city stands on twelve foundations, and the SIXTH is sardius — the stone whose color is the color of blood. Without the blood of the Lamb (Rev 5:9; 7:14), there is no city. The same red-stone that named the church of Sardis ("thou hast a name that thou livest, and art dead" — Rev 3:1) preaches a warning: even the city named for the blood-red stone can be dead if her people do not actually drink the blood of Christ. Sardius is the stone of Christ's blood — and that blood is either a foundation or a witness against you.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A deep red precious stone (carnelian); sixth foundation of the New Jerusalem and the red half of God's appearance on the throne.

SARDIUS, noun. A precious stone of a deep red color, identified today as carnelian or red jasper. Named after Sardis in Asia Minor where it was anciently mined.

In Scripture, the sixth foundation of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:20); the first stone of the high priest's breastplate (Exod 28:17); a stone covering the anointed cherub in Eden (Ezek 28:13); the red half of the appearance of God on the throne (Rev 4:3).

📖 Key Scripture

Revelation 21:20 — "The fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite."

Revelation 4:3 — "And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald."

Exodus 28:17 — "And thou shalt set in it settings of stones, even four rows of stones: the first row shall be a sardius, a topaz, and a carbuncle: this shall be the first row."

Ezekiel 28:13 — "Thou hast been in Eden the garden of God; every precious stone was thy covering, the sardius, topaz, and the diamond, the beryl, the onyx, and the jasper."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Sardius is corrupted when the blood-red theology of the stone is stripped (its connection to atonement and wrath dissolved into mere color choice), or when modern commentaries detach Revelation 4:3 from its OT roots in priestly representation.

expand to see more

Atonement-shy theology. The blood-red of sardius testifies to the price of approach to God. Modern liberal theology, allergic to substitutionary atonement, often refuses to read color symbolism in Scripture this way — preferring abstract "love" or "presence" categories. But the priest carried sardius FIRST, before all other stones, when he approached the holy place. The stone preaches: approach to God is purchased in blood. To remove that is to remove the gospel.

On the other side, some treat sardius and the other stones as raw decorative inventory rather than as theologically loaded. The biblical stones are NOT neutral. Each was chosen, ordered, and placed by the Spirit. Sardius opens the high priest's breastplate; sardius half-defines the appearance of God on the throne; sardius founds the sixth course of the eternal city. Three places in canon — and all three carry the weight of red, blood, and approach. To shrug at this is to read a flatter Bible than the one God wrote.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

Greek sardios (G4556), Hebrew odem (H124) — a deep blood-red carnelian or red jasper; named for Sardis in Asia Minor.

expand to see more

Greek sardios (G4556) — sardius/sardine stone; sixth foundation of New Jerusalem, red half of God's appearance (Rev 4:3)

Hebrew odem (H124) — sardius; from adam (red, ground) — same root as the name Adam, the red-earth man

Named for Sardis in Asia Minor (one of the seven churches, Rev 3:1) where the stone was mined

Likely modern equivalent: carnelian or red jasper; the deep-red translucent variety

Usage

"The sixth foundation is sardius — the blood-red stone, the price of every step into God's city."

"On God's throne shines sardius and jasper: justice and glory, wrath and light, never separated."

"The high priest entered the holy place wearing sardius first — no approach to God without the cost the stone foretells."
